title: Astronauts and rockets
examples: What do astronauts wear when they go to space?
How does a rocket get off the ground?
Why do things float in space?

explain.say: Today we will learn about astronauts and rockets.
Now look! Here it is in 3D: the stages of a rocket. Can you see the escape tower and the crew capsule? Tap any part, and I will tell you about it.
Astronauts wear special suits for space.
When astronauts float in space, there is no gravity.
Blast off is when the rocket starts moving fast.
In space, things float because there is little gravity.
A real life example is jumping in a swimming pool.

faq.q: Why do astronauts float in space?
faq.a: They float because space has very little gravity pulling things down. It is like being in a giant bubble where nothing pulls you to the floor.
asks: Why don't they fall down in space?

faq.q: What is the main job of a space suit?
faq.a: The space suit keeps the astronaut alive by providing air and keeping them safe from space's cold. It is like a personal bubble of air.
asks: Why do astronauts need big suits?
What does the suit do for them?

faq.q: How does a rocket actually blast off?
faq.a: A rocket blasts off by burning fuel very fast to create a huge push called thrust. This push sends the rocket upward into space.
asks: What makes a rocket go fast?
How does it leave the ground?
What is thrust in a rocket?

faq.q: Is floating the same as zero gravity?
faq.a: Floating is what happens because of low gravity, which is close to zero gravity. It means objects just drift slowly.
asks: What is the difference between floating and zero gravity?
Is low gravity the same as no gravity?

faq.q: What is the difference between a rocket and a spacecraft?
faq.a: A rocket is the vehicle that provides the power to blast off. The spacecraft is the whole vehicle that takes astronauts to their destination.
asks: Is the rocket the whole thing?

facts: Space suits provide breathable air for astronauts.
Rockets create upward motion using powerful thrust.
Floating happens because gravity is very weak in space.
Astronauts must be trained for long missions.

quiz.say: What provides the necessary air for astronauts in space?
quiz.why: The oxygen tank is part of the suit and holds the air the astronaut needs to breathe.

wrong.0: The helmet protects the face but does not provide the main air supply.
wrong.1: The seal keeps air in, but the tank provides the air itself.
wrong.2: The suit is the whole thing, but the tank is the specific part for air.

quiz.say: What force makes a rocket move off the ground?
quiz.why: Thrust is the big push created by burning fuel that moves the rocket upward.

wrong.1: Weight is the pull down by gravity, which the rocket must overcome.
wrong.2: Gravity is the force pulling it down, not the force pushing it up.
wrong.3: Fuel is what is burned, but thrust is the resulting push.

quiz.say: When astronauts float, what is the main reason?
quiz.why: Floating happens because the pull of gravity is very weak in space.

wrong.0: Wind is an atmosphere force, not the reason for floating in space.
wrong.2: Water resistance only happens when you are in a liquid.
wrong.3: Lack of air is dangerous; floating is due to low gravity.
